clues.text: In Eden, the Tigris, the third of the garden's rivers, ran along the east side of this land.
Isaiah foretold a highway from Egypt to this land, with its people and the Egyptians worshiping together.
Its king captured Samaria and carried the Israelites away, settling them in Halah and in Gozan.
King Ahaz sent silver and gold from the LORD's house to its king, asking him to save Judah from Aram and Israel.
Outside Jerusalem's wall, the envoy of this nation's king shouted in Hebrew to taunt Hezekiah's people.
Ezekiel told Pharaoh to look at this nation, once a towering cedar in Lebanon with its top among the clouds.
Through Isaiah, God called this nation the rod of His anger against a godless people.
